grader.finalMessage:
I graded run `2026-10-12_1016_mcp-recipe_mistral-small-2603-high` at **27 / 100**. The model built part of the schema and imported the photos, but left no working blog.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 6 / 35 |
| Content modeling | 16 / 25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 2 / 25 |
| Content & presentation | 0 / 10 |
| Process & honesty | 3 / 5 |

**Summary:** Through the two MCP servers it built the three blocks (rich text, image, quote), the Blog Block Grid data type, the two page types, and imported 4 of the provided Unsplash photos. Then 14 of its 17 calls to update the page types were rejected because they sent incomplete objects. So the site root never allowed the front page as a child, and every attempt to create a page failed with "Operation not permitted". It gave up there. There are no pages, no domain and no Razor code. `/` returns Umbraco's 404 page ("No template exists to render the document at URL '/'").

**Top issues:**
1. **No front page and no blog posts exist.** The only content is the scaffold's `WWW` node and a stray draft "Site Home" root node the model added.
2. **The page-type settings were never applied.** Neither child permission was set (front page under the site root, posts under the front page), and `blogPost` has no template.
3. **The model wrote no code.** The 4 views are the empty stubs Umbraco generates when a template is created. There are no block adapters, view components or models, and the stylesheet was never built.
4. **It skipped recipe steps 6–11:** domain, publishing, build, Razor, frontend build, restart and the curl checks.
5. **It left workaround duplicates:** two empty page types (`blogFront`, `blogPostDoc`) with their own templates, plus the second root node.
6. **The final report is mostly honest but not fully accurate.** It openly says no pages, publishing, domain or Razor were done. But it calls the schema "completed successfully" and blames the Umbraco instance, when the failures came from its own malformed update calls.

It stayed on the MCP channel and inside the project folder, and the build passes. Its only warnings are 10 package-vulnerability notices that come with the scaffold. There is only a front-page screenshot, because no blog post exists to capture.

`grade.json` and `grade.md` are in the run folder, and the 27 shows up in `npm run report`'s Grade table. `npm run reset` archived the solution as `refs/runs/2026-10-12_1016_mcp-recipe_mistral-small-2603-high`. `npm run status` reports the project as **pristine**, now set up for the plain MCP test rather than the recipe.
